enriched_description: Flowing robe-like outer garment with full-length loose-fitting silhouette extending to ankles. Wide bell-shaped sleeves with pointed or rounded edges. Fabric typically matte black polyester or wool with smooth drape. Distinctive colored velvet panels or bars on sleeves indicating academic degree level. Front opening with closure at neck. Shoulder yoke with pointed or rounded shape. Proportions: sleeve width significantly exceeding arm width creating voluminous appearance. Hem width creating triangular silhouette when viewed from front. Trim color and pattern varies by institution.

Portable rectangular box-shaped instrument with expandable pleated bellows at center. Piano-style keyboard or button array on right-hand casing. Bass button grid on left-hand casing. Bellows constructed from folded cardboard or leather with fabric edges creating zigzag profile when expanded. Hard shell casing typically glossy black or pearl finish. Metal reed plates visible through decorative grille. Shoulder straps attached at top corners. Proportions: bellows width when compressed approximately equal to casing depth. Overall rectangular form with bellows creating accordion-like folded texture. Decorative inlay patterns on casing surface.

Hollow wooden body with figure-eight silhouette featuring rounded upper and lower bouts connected by narrow waist. Circular sound hole centered on top plate with decorative rosette ring. Six strings running from bridge at lower body to headstock. Fretted fingerboard with metal fret wires and position markers. Wooden neck with smooth satin or gloss finish. Headstock with six tuning pegs arranged three-per-side. Bridge with saddle and string pins. Body surface with glossy varnish showing wood grain patterns. Proportions: body length approximately 1.5x neck length. Sound hole diameter approximately one-third of body width.

Massive flat-top naval vessel with expansive rectangular flight deck spanning entire ship length. Deck surface dark gray non-slip coating with painted runway markings and landing guide lines. Island superstructure positioned starboard side with radar arrays and communication antennas. Catapult tracks visible on bow section. Arresting gear wires spanning deck width. Hangar bay beneath flight deck with elevator platforms. Hull with gray military paint and visible waterline. Proportions: flight deck length significantly exceeding beam width creating elongated rectangular profile. Island structure height approximately one-fifth of ship length. Deck edge safety nets visible along perimeter.

Tubular cylindrical fuselage with rounded nose cone and tapered tail section. Low-mounted swept-back wings with winglets at tips. Jet engines mounted beneath wings in cylindrical nacelles. Vertical stabilizer (tail fin) with airline livery markings. Horizontal stabilizers mounted on tail cone. Passenger windows in linear row along fuselage sides. Landing gear with multiple wheel assemblies. Fuselage surface smooth metallic or painted finish with airline branding. Proportions: wingspan approximately equal to fuselage length. Engine diameter approximately one-tenth of fuselage diameter. Tail fin height approximately one-fifth of fuselage length.

Elongated cigar-shaped gas-filled envelope with smooth taut fabric surface. Streamlined aerodynamic profile with rounded nose and tapered tail. Gondola or cabin suspended beneath envelope front section. Vertical and horizontal stabilizer fins at tail forming cruciform or H-shaped configuration. Propeller nacelles mounted on envelope sides or gondola. Mooring mast attachment point at nose. Envelope surface typically silver or white with painted markings. Proportions: envelope length 4-6x envelope diameter creating elongated cylindrical form. Gondola length approximately one-fifth of envelope length. Fin span approximately one-quarter of envelope length.

Raised rectangular platform or table structure with flat horizontal top surface. Constructed from stone, wood, or marble with polished or carved finish. Front panel often decorated with religious iconography, carvings, or inlaid patterns. Steps or platform base elevating surface above floor level. Ornamental elements including candles, crosses, or ceremonial objects on surface. Surface material typically smooth polished stone or wood with reflective quality. Proportions: table height approximately waist-level (0.9-1.2m). Length significantly exceeding width creating rectangular form. Decorative front panel height approximately two-thirds of total height.

Box-shaped van chassis with raised modular body compartment. White or high-visibility color scheme with reflective striping and emergency markings. Emergency light bar mounted on roof with red and blue lenses. Side compartments with roll-up or hinged doors. Rear double doors with window panels. Cross or Star of Life emblem visible on sides. Cab section integrated with box body creating stepped profile. Proportions: box body height approximately 1.5x cab height. Overall length dominated by rear compartment. Reflective chevron patterns on rear surface. Window placement limited to cab and rear doors.

Flat-bottomed hull design with boat-like V-shaped or flat underside for water navigation. Wheeled chassis integrated with hull structure for land mobility. Waterproof body seams and sealed compartments. Propeller or water jet visible at stern for aquatic propulsion. Standard automotive features (wheels, steering, windshield) for land operation. Hull surface typically painted with marine-grade coating. Transition features between land and water modes visible. Proportions: hull width broader than typical vehicle creating stable water platform. Height increased due to hull depth. Wheel placement optimized for both land and water stability.

Circular face with flat dial surface displaying numbered hour markers (1-12) or Roman numerals. Three rotating hands (hour, minute, second) of varying lengths mounted at center pivot. Hour hand shortest and widest, minute hand longer and narrower, second hand thinnest. Dial surface typically white or light-colored with high-contrast markings. Outer rim or bezel framing the dial surface. Glass or plastic crystal covering the face. Mounting hardware visible on back or sides. Proportions: minute hand length approximately 80% of dial radius. Hour hand length approximately 60% of dial radius. Bezel width approximately 10% of total diameter.
